x̅j : mean of jth treatment,

x̅ : (T)/(N) where N = Sigmaj₌₁^kn_j and T : Total of all observation,

Then the sum of squares within groups (SSW) is calculated as:

Σj=1kΣi=1nj(xij−x¯j)2

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** Sum of Squares Within Groups (SSW):

__
 
• SSW measures the variability within each treatment group.
 
• It is calculated by summing the squared differences between each observation and its treatment group mean.
 
• **The formula Σj=1kΣi=1nj(xij−x¯j)2" id="MathJax-Element-718-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">Σkj=1Σnji=1(xij−x¯j)2Σj=1kΣi=1nj(xij−x¯j)2" id="MathJax-Element-297-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">Σkj=1Σnji=1(xij−x¯j)2Σj=1kΣi=1nj(xij−x¯j)2
 Σj=1kΣi=1nj(xij−x¯j)2
 \rm \Sigma_{j=1}^k \Sigma_{i=1}^{n_j}(x_{ij}-\bar x_j)² correctly represents this calculation.**
 
• This formula ensures that we capture the variation within each group and not between groups.
